data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Gula was the goddess of the moon and the protector of the harvest. However, in the context of Christian names, Gula is often associated with greed and covetousness. The name Gula carries the meaning “Greedy, covetous” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. in_greek.name: Γουλά
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek form of the Hebrew name 'Gula'. It is found in the New Testament in the book of Luke (7:36-50) where it is used to refer to the sinful woman who anointed Jesus' feet with her tears and ointment.

in_latin.name: Gula
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin form of the Greek name 'Γουλά'. It was not widely used as a given name in the Latin world, but it is found in some medieval sources and in the works of certain saints.

in_english.name: Gula
